claim: On fresh seeds 22-23 at N=128 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the final best-layer force margin is 0.108 (seed 22, layer 1, R2 0.569 vs control 0.461) and 0.094 (seed 23, layer 1, R2 0.562 vs control 0.468). That is 0.139-0.140 below the matched N=64 seeds (0.247/0.234) and well above N=256 (0.033-0.040). Seed 23 never reaches the 0.1 bar, and seed 22 crosses it only at step 2500. accel_step is decoded much better: layer-4 R2 0.894/0.898 vs controls 0.677/0.725, giving raw margins 0.217/0.174 and headroom-normalised margins 0.67/0.63, against about 0.68/0.71 at N=64. Force's normalised margin is only about 0.20/0.18.
confidence_note: Both completed seeds meet every expected-if-true condition. Force is in [0.08, 0.20] and at least 0.04 below the same seed's N=64 value, and normalised accel_step is in [0.62, 0.77], so the gradual decline of force with steps_per_orbit replicates on new seeds. Caveats: (1) Both values sit near the low end of the predicted band and below seeds 20-21 at N=128 (0.150/0.131). With 4 seeds the N=128 range is 0.094-0.150, and seed 23 would not count as a beats-control force result on its own. A seed below 0.08 or above 0.20 in further N=128 runs would weaken the 'intermediate' claim. (2) The force drop comes from lower trained R2 (0.56-0.57 vs 0.68-0.70 at N=64), not from higher controls (0.46-0.47 vs about 0.45). This makes it a real decodability difference, but the force signal still sits at layer 1, the distance layer, and has not been tested with distance regressed out. (3) Force is still rising at step 3000 (about +0.004-0.006 per 500 steps, val_mse_ratio 0.067-0.079), so the N=64 vs N=128 gap holds only at matched training length. (4) Normalised accel_step is a little lower at N=128 (0.63-0.67) than at N=64 (0.68-0.71). That fits the predicted range, but 'flat across N' would be in doubt if more seeds widen this gap.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-055140-2cc5 (issue 0): Accepted. The 0.033-0.040 N=256 values come from the original runs (f-20261013-000253-c709), and the current pipeline has replaced them. Under the current pipeline, N=256 at 3000 steps gives force 0.1132 (seed 20) and 0.0032 (seed 21), and two identical reruns confirm this (f-20261013-050513-2c7a, f-20261013-054603-d6cc). Seed 20's N=256 margin is therefore higher than both N=128 seeds 22-23 (0.108/0.094), so 'well above N=256' is false as written. The correct statement is that the N=256 comparison is unresolved: the two current-pipeline N=256 seeds span 0.003-0.113, which brackets the N=128 seeds 22-23 values. The expected_if_false anchor '<=0.06, close to N=256' also rested on the old numbers. The verdict depends only on the [0.08, 0.20] band and the >= 0.04 drop from same-seed N=64 (0.247/0.234 vs 0.108/0.094), and both still hold in both seeds, so the replicated status stands for the N=64-vs-N=128 claim alone. Nothing in this finding should be read as an N=128 vs N=256 ordering. This cycle runs N=256 seeds 22-25 under the current pipeline, with seeds 22-23 paired against this N=128 arm, to settle whether N=256 force really is lower than N=128.

Response to review r-20261013-055140-2cc5 (issue 0): Accepted. The N=256 anchor of 0.033-0.040 comes from the original runs (f-20261013-000253-c709). The current pipeline is shown deterministic by f-20261013-050513-2c7a and f-20261013-054603-d6cc, and under it N=256 at 3000 steps gives force margins of 0.113 (seed 20) and 0.003 (seed 21). Seed 20's N=256 value is higher than both N=128 seeds 22-23 (0.108 and 0.094). So the claim's 'well above N=256 (0.033-0.040)' is unsupported, and so is the expected_if_false anchor '<=0.06, close to N=256'. The correct statement: N=128 seeds 22-23 sit 0.139-0.140 below their matched N=64 seeds. Their relation to N=256 is not established, because N=256 has not been run for seeds 22-23 under the current pipeline, and the two current-pipeline N=256 seeds that do exist (20 and 21) bracket the N=128 values. The verdict rests only on the [0.08, 0.20] band and the N=64 comparison, so it is unaffected and the status stays. This cycle runs N=256 for seeds 22-23 on data_seed 0, and for seeds 20-21 on data_seed 1, using current-pipeline runs only, so the N=128 vs N=256 contrast can be measured per seed. Earlier findings citing N=256 force of 0.03-0.04 as the endpoint (f-20261013-015914-3f49, f-20261013-015951-62c7 and the 'about 0.1 per doubling' description) should be read with the same correction.
